title: Rerr.error_code stored as u8 instead of RerrCode enum
description:
File: rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs
Line: 487

The `Rerr` struct stores `error_code: u8` despite validating against `RerrCode` enum during parsing (line 511-513). This creates drift risk: if a new `RerrCode` variant is added, the struct field accepts any u8 value even though only validated variants pass parsing.

Bad outcome: Future maintainer adds `RerrCode::TemporaryFailure = 2`, updates `from_u8()`, but now `Rerr.error_code` can be 0, 1, or 2 while code elsewhere might only handle 0 and 1.

Fix: Change `error_code: u8` to `error_code: RerrCode` in the struct. This makes the type system enforce that only valid codes are stored.
close_reason: Fixed in rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs: Rerr.error_code is now RerrCode instead of u8. Investigation note: the bead claims parsing already validated via RerrCode::from_u8 at lines 511-513 — that code does not exist at HEAD (no RerrCode anywhere in git history); the enum had to be created. Design constrained by cross-implementation reality: canonical vector rerr_max_error_code carries error_code=255 ('maximum value for single-byte error code') and must round-trip, and the C + Python reference impls parse error_code verbatim — so a closed enum that rejects unknown codes would violate test-vector parity. Implemented open typed enum: RerrCode::{Unspecified=wire 0, NoRoute=wire 1, Other(u8)} with total From<u8> and lossless From<RerrCode> for u8 conversions; parse maps data[1] through From, write_to serializes back through Into, giving bit-exact wire round-trip for all 256 values. Type system now enforces that only valid codes are stored while future variants (e.g. TemporaryFailure=2) can be added by extending from_u8 mapping without any u8 leakage into the struct. Tests added: rerr_code_wire_roundtrip_all_values (exhaustive 256-value wire-identity oracle), rerr_canonical_vectors (hardcoded hex from test/vectors/loadng_messages.json: NoRoute/Other(255)/Other(2)+flags 0x80). Existing rerr_roundtrip updated to RerrCode::NoRoute. No external Rust users of Rerr.error_code exist (grepped workspace). Verified: cargo test -p lichen-core --lib = 269 passed 0 failed.
